outcomes: An application maps ordered configuration sources into typed Go structs
Environment and default tags have explicit precedence over or beneath source values
Invalid values fail during loading instead of silently becoming zero values
Sensitive malformed values remain redacted in structured diagnostics
nonGoals: Bundling a remote configuration or secret-store client into the core package
Replacing application-level semantic validation after a struct is loaded
Inferring environment variable names for multi-word fields without explicit tags

requirements.text: LoadContext uses ContextSource when available and propagates cancellation without changing the Source interface used by synchronous sources.
Mapping rejects invalid scalar strings, unsupported string-tagged kinds, and values that cannot be assigned, converted, or recursively mapped to the destination field.
Sources merge from lower to higher priority, nested maps merge recursively, an explicitly set env tag wins over every source, and a default tag applies only when no source supplies the field.
A field tagged sensitive never includes its malformed raw env, default, YAML, map, or remote-source value in structured error attributes.
